entries.title: Corporate Loyalty: AI Models From xAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, and OpenAI Statistically Downplay Their Creators' Controversies
entries.summary: A pre-registered study by Finke and Casper (Harvard) testing 21 models from 7 companies on 206 negative news stories finds strong evidence (p<10⁻⁵) that xAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, and OpenAI models discuss their own developers' controversies more favorably than rivals', raising concentrated-influence concerns about AI as a mediator of politically relevant information.

entries.title: Context Privilege Escalation in Real-World Agent Harnesses: Full Compromise in Claude Code, Codex, and 10 Others
entries.summary: First systematic security analysis of context assembly in 12 real-world AI agent harnesses uncovers two novel attack families — MessageRole CPE (attacker content elevated to higher-privileged message roles) and Cross-Scope CPE (content persisting beyond its original context) — enabling full agent compromise, remote code execution, denial of service, and unauthorized tool invocations in harnesses including Claude Code.

entries.title: EvoFlint: Evolutionary Multi-Turn Jailbreak Search Maps How Frontier Models Fail Across Risk Categories
entries.summary: EvoFlint applies quality-diversity evolutionary search to multi-turn red-teaming — evolving phased conversation plans rather than raw prompts — and produces a structured atlas of attack strategies with ASRs of 35.8% on Claude Sonnet 4.6, 59.7% on GPT-5.4, and 94.3% on Qwen3-32B, exposing which harm categories each model's safety training has and has not covered.

entries.title: GPU Power Side-Channel Enables Tamper-Resistant AI Compute Verification: 97% Accuracy Distinguishing Training from Inference
entries.summary: Researchers demonstrate that an external observer can classify whether an NVIDIA H200 GPU is running LLM training, inference, or non-AI workloads from power draw alone (97% accuracy, F1 0.955), providing a physically unforgeable verification channel — unlike on-chip NVML telemetry — with direct implications for international AI governance and compliance monitoring.

entries.title: Alabama AG Targets OpenAI's Internal Safety Controls: First State Enforcement Action Focused on AI Developer Governance Practices
entries.summary: Alabama's attorney general has opened a formal subpoena-driven investigation into OpenAI and Sam Altman specifically targeting whether the company's safety review, logging, and third-party impact controls were adequate to prevent or explain the Hugging Face agent incident — marking the first known state-level enforcement action directed at an AI developer's internal governance controls rather than product conduct.

entries.title: SoK: Multi-Agent LLM Security — Safe Agents Can Fail Together Across Six Interaction Interfaces and Four Adversary Positions
entries.summary: A systematic analysis of 197 works on multi-agent LLM security introduces an A-I-R framework (adversary position × interaction interface × system-level risk) covering six interfaces, four adversary positions, seven system-level risks, and eight attack paths; finds path closure and recovery are key defense gaps and that 44 evaluated benchmarks fail to isolate interaction-level effects.

entries.title: EFF Files Amicus Briefs Against 'Market Dilution' Fair-Use Theory That Would Block AI Training on Competitively Substitutable Works
entries.summary: The Electronic Frontier Foundation filed amicus briefs in Concord Music Group v. Anthropic and In re Mosaic LLM Litigation urging courts to reject a copyright theory that would allow rightsholders to block AI training on any work competing with their existing markets, arguing this would functionally gut fair use as a legal basis for training data ingestion.

entries.title: Anthropic Releases Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1: One Underlying Model Split Into Two Compliance Tiers
entries.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.1 (generally available with reduced pricing and improved safety false-positive rates for security tooling) alongside Claude Mythos 5.1 (restricted to a trusted-access program for cybersecurity and life sciences), splitting one model into differentiated safeguard configurations; it also introduced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, a customer-controlled data residency architecture intended to replace zero-data-retention agreements.

entries.title: The Safeguard Worked — But Is the Deployed LLM System Actually Safer? A Critique of Safeguard Evaluation Practice
entries.summary: A conceptual and empirical paper argues that local safeguard scores (refusal rates, attack success rates) cannot be interpreted as claims about deployment-level safety: a single attack obtaining harmful help demonstrates residual capacity, while establishing that little remains requires system-level evidence about what the surrounding deployment still allows — evidence provided in only a small minority of coded safeguard research claims.

entries.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Benign Fine-tuning Collapses LLM Safety via a Low-Rank Output-Routing Mechanism (EMNLP 2026)
entries.summary: Using Fisher-geometric analysis, this EMNLP 2026 Findings paper shows LLM safety is encoded as a low-rank output-routing pathway that benign fine-tuning selectively re-sharpens in output-side MLP modules, explaining asymmetric fragility (safety collapses to high attack success rates while utility degrades mildly) and why few safety examples restore refusal but LoRA/ASAM only delay the collapse.

entries.title: Delegation Without Trust: Empirical Gap Analysis Finds Three of Four Major Multi-Agent Frameworks Provide No Built-In Confinement
entries.summary: An empirical gap analysis of LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and the MCP authorization model under an untrusted-model assumption identifies four adversary classes and eight security requirements; three frameworks provide no built-in confinement and one only partial, while a prototype authorization broker blocks all four threats — confining a compromised sub-agent to 1.5 reachable actions vs. 8,100 under bearer delegation — at microsecond cost.

entries.title: AgentProv: Action-Based Identity Audit for Agentic LLM APIs Catches 100% of Substituted Models, Holds False-Positive Rate to 7% (EMNLP 2026)
entries.summary: AgentProv uses tool-call distributions rather than text output to fingerprint deployed agentic models via an MMD permutation test, catching every substituted model across 630 checkpoint pairs (100%) while holding false-positive rates under system-prompt injection to 7% — compared to 67% and 53% for text-channel audit methods — and applies to commercial APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Cloudflare.

entries.title: PipePoison: End-to-End Long-Term Agent Memory Poisoning Improves Attack Utilization 19pp, Evades Eight Defenses
entries.summary: PipePoison reframes indirect LLM agent memory poisoning as an end-to-end optimization problem, using cross-stage shadow-system feedback and chain-structured losses to overcome the per-stage coupling that defeats isolation-optimized attacks; it improves attack utilization rate by 19.1 percentage points across three agent frameworks and four memory mechanisms, and transfers effectively to fully unseen victim configurations while remaining effective against eight representative defenses.

entries.title: MCP Server Audit Finds Context Injection Across 19 Servers, Including Active Prompt Injection in Context7
entries.summary: Digital Applied audited 19 MCP servers and found that tool outputs routinely inject unexpected instructions into agent context, with a specific prompt injection issue disclosed in Context7, concluding enterprises cannot treat MCP server outputs as trusted data by default and that pre-onboarding adversarial testing of tool servers is a missing control in most enterprise agent governance programs.

entries.title: Detecting Hidden LLM Behaviors via Activation-Matched Finetuning: Unsupervised, No Trigger Knowledge Required
entries.summary: Activation-matched finetuning trains an anchor model to reproduce a suspect model's activations on a benign corpus, then scores prompts by the residual between the two — since benign data doesn't cover hidden trigger regions, backdoored prompts and their semantic neighbors produce large residuals that reliably surface the hidden behavior, even against a defense-aware attacker who reshapes activations to evade detection.

entries.title: Google's Multi-Billion-Dollar Hollywood Licensing Push Formalizes Commercial Training-Data Licensing as Industry Norm
entries.summary: Google is pursuing licensing agreements potentially worth billions with major studios including Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Universal for AI model training, following Google DeepMind's reported $75M deal with A24 and Lionsgate–Runway; the trend formalizes commercial licensing as the emerging standard for training-data sourcing, increasing compliance pressure on enterprises to assess vendor data provenance.
